title: Why does toast land butter-side down?
caption:
Blame the table, not the butter. 🍞🧈

Toast sliding off a normal table (about 75 cm) only has time for roughly half a turn before it hits the floor, so the buttered side ends up underneath. Physicist Robert Matthews worked it out in 1995 (European Journal of Physics) and won the 1996 Ig Nobel Prize in Physics for it. The butter itself is at most about 10 % of a 40 g slice and barely matters.

In a school experiment with nearly 10,000 drops, 62 % landed butter-down. To get a full turn and land butter-up, the table would need to be about 3 metres tall.

Send this to the friend who blames bad luck every time breakfast hits the floor.
